title: Exposing Weaknesses in Emotion Recognition in Conversations
abstract: arXiv:2609.05806v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Emotion Recognition in Conversations (ERC) aims to identify speakers' emotions in multi-turn dialogue. Accurate emotion recognition can support a wide range of applications, including empathetic conversational agents, mental health support, and educational technologies. While many recent approaches rely on task-specific fine-tuning, such models may exploit dataset-specific cues. A central yet rarely questioned assumption in ERC is that each utterance can be assigned a single unambiguous emotion label. To investigate this assumption, we study ERC using Large Language Models (LLMs) in a zero-shot setting while incorporating preceding conversational turns as context. We show that aggregate metrics mask systematic failures. Errors concentrate around utterances containing negations, exclamations, and interjections. translated_title: 揭示对话情绪识别中的弱点
translated_abstract: 对话情绪识别（ERC）旨在识别多轮对话中说话人的情绪。准确的情绪识别可以支持广泛的应用，包括共情对话代理、心理健康支持和教育技术。虽然许多近期方法依赖于特定任务的微调，但此类模型可能会利用数据集特有的线索。ERC中一个核心却很少被质疑的假设是：每条话语都可以被赋予一个单一且明确的情绪标签。为了探究这一假设，我们使用大语言模型（LLM）在零样本设置下研究ERC，并将先前的对话轮次作为上下文纳入。我们表明，总体指标掩盖了系统性的失败。错误集中在包含否定词、感叹词和感叹语的话语上。这一模式在所有被评估的模型中都保持一致，这表明问题源于基准数据集的局限性，而非特定模型的弱点。
tldr: 该研究通过零样本大语言模型实验，揭示了对话情绪识别基准中“每条话语仅有单一情绪标签”这一假设的缺陷——错误集中在含否定词、感叹词和感叹语的话语上，且在各模型间表现一致，说明问题源于数据集本身而非模型。
en_tdlr: This study uses zero-shot LLM experiments to expose the flawed assumption in ERC benchmarks that each utterance has a single unambiguous emotion label, showing consistent errors on utterances with negations, exclamations, and interjections across models, indicating benchmark limitations rather than model-specific weaknesses.
